definitions.explanation: A system for organizing days and months, or a physical calendar or almanac. Often refers to the traditional Japanese calendar system and its seasonal divisions.

examples.japanese: {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}ではもう{春|はる}だ。
examples.english: According to the calendar, it's already spring.

examples.japanese: {旧暦|きゅうれき}の{暦|こよみ}では{正月|しょうがつ}は{二月|にがつ}ごろになる。
examples.english: In the old calendar, New Year falls around February.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎年|まいとし}{暦|こよみ}を{見|み}て、{農作業|のうさぎょう}の{時期|じき}を{決|き}めていた。
examples.english: My grandmother would check the almanac every year to decide when to do the farm work.

notes:
Refers to both the concept of a calendar system and a physical calendar or almanac. While カレンダー is the everyday word for a wall/desk calendar, {暦|こよみ} carries a more traditional, cultural nuance and is often associated with the old lunar calendar and seasonal markers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では — according to the calendar
- {旧暦|きゅうれき}の{暦|こよみ} — the old (lunar) calendar
- {暦|こよみ}を{見|み}る — to check the almanac
- {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}の{春|はる} — spring by the calendar (but not yet in reality)

RELATED WORDS:
- カレンダー — calendar (modern wall/desk calendar)
- {旧暦|きゅうれき} — old/lunar calendar
- {新暦|しんれき} — new/Gregorian calendar
- {二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき} — the 24 solar terms (traditional seasonal divisions)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1873, but the old lunar calendar ({旧暦|きゅうれき}) still influences festivals and seasonal customs. The phrase {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では is commonly used when the calendar date says one season but the weather feels like another.
